exact_claim: The 2026 Consumer White Paper (cabinet decision 2026-06-12) reports that about 20% ('約2割') of people who use subscription services had experienced trouble when cancelling.
population: Subscription users among CAA survey respondents (exact base UNKNOWN)
denominator: UNKNOWN (work-order lead says subscription users among prior-year online purchasers; not confirmed)
exact_locator: White paper chapter/figure UNKNOWN; media headlines 2026-06-12
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): 'SNS相談が最多更新の10万件 サブスク解約、2割トラブル経験' (Kyodo headline); Nikkei: 'サブスク解約トラブル2割が経験'.
counterevidence: None found. No independent survey with a comparable probability sample was located.
limitation: All three outlets re-report one release (family F01). 'Trouble' is undefined in the extracts. Incidence of trouble is not demand, delegation or willingness to pay.
decision_use: A1: directional only. A minority of users report cancellation friction. Not used for sizing or adoption.

exact_claim: The work-order lead figures 71.6% (subscription-contract experience among prior-year online purchasers) and 17.9% (cancellation trouble among subscription users) were not found in any search extract.
exact_locator: Targeted searches for '"17.9%" サブスク 解約' and '"71.6%" サブスクリプション' on 2026-10-05
supporting_passage: No extract contained either figure.
counterevidence: '約2割' is consistent with 17.9% after rounding, but consistency is not confirmation.
limitation: The primary PDF is blocked. The survey round, n, fielding dates, age structure and question wording are all unconfirmed.
decision_use: Neither figure is used anywhere in this packet. E-queue: open the white paper and its underlying survey.

exact_claim: Among people who reported cancellation trouble, the most-cited problems were 'could not find the cancellation page / it was deep in the site' (46.0%) and 'the procedure was complicated / had more steps than necessary' (45.7%).
metric: Share citing each problem (multiple answers presumed)
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): '「解約手続きページが見つからなかった/ウェブサイトの深い階層にあった」が46.0%、「手続きが複雑だった/必要以上に多かった」が45.7%'.
counterevidence: None found. Other answer options and their shares were not visible, e.g. phone-only or retention pressure.
limitation: One family. The full option list is unknown, so it is not known whether phone-only, in-person or 'charged after cancelling' were offered as options.
decision_use: A2/H02 (against): the top-cited friction is J3 (finding the route), which a guide or deep link (C02) addresses without execution. Complexity (45.7%) is J3/J4 and ambiguous.

exact_claim: PIO-NET recorded 98,189 (2022), 80,302 (2023) and 89,044 (2024) consultations about mail-order 定期購入 (recurring purchase) contracts. A CAA release reports 89,893 for 2024.
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): Kokusen: '2022年 98,189件, 2023年 80,302件, 2024年 89,044件'; ecnomikata: '2024年の通信販売の「定期購入」に関する相談件数は8万9893件'.
counterevidence: The two 2024 figures differ by 849 (0.95%), probably because of different PIO-NET cut-off dates. Not resolved.
limitation: Consultations are not consumers or incidents. 定期購入 covers physical-product recurring purchases, mostly trial-to-subscription traps, not digital subscriptions. Both figures come from PIO-NET (one underlying dataset).
decision_use: A1: the largest observable complaint pocket is 定期購入 at about 80-98k a year, roughly an order of magnitude above Kokusen's coded 'サブスク' consultations (R7-E-A08).

exact_claim: Kokusen describes 定期購入 trouble as skewing toward people in their 50s and older and toward cosmetics, with a typical pattern of 'the ad said cancel any time, but the phone line does not connect'.
exact_locator: Kokusen subscription_traps; 見守り新鮮情報 504
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): '「いつでも解約できる」と書いてあったのに…電話がつながらず、なかなか解約できない'; '年代別では50代以上、商品別では化粧品が多い'; advice: '解約の期日までに事業者に連絡がつかない不安がある場合は、電話やメールの発信履歴など連絡した証拠を残し'.
limitation: No shares or counts were visible, so the skew cannot be quantified.
decision_use: Identifies a concrete J4 friction architecture: a phone-only channel plus a deadline before the next shipment. Candidate route class C or D. Tested in S4/S5.

exact_claim: Japan's consumer centres received 1.006M consultations in FY2025, versus 913k in FY2024. Contract parties aged 70+ were 25.6%; those aged 65+ numbered 330,497 (37.7%).
metric: Count; age share of contract party
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): '2025年度の相談件数は100.6万件で、2024年度の91.3万件に比べ約９万件増加'; '70歳以上の割合が最も高く、25.6%'; '65歳以上…330,497件…37.7％'.
limitation: Covers all consultation topics, not subscriptions. Consultation propensity varies by age, so this measures who complains to centres, not who has the problem.
decision_use: Comparator only: the 65+ share of consultations (37.7%) is above the 65+ share of the population (29.4%, R7-E-A07); ratio 1.28 (R7-E-A15). This hints at a family-assisted senior segment but is not subscription-specific.

exact_claim: People aged 65 and over were 29.4% of Japan's population in 2025 (36.19M).
exact_locator: Statistics Bureau 統計トピックス (敬老の日), exact topics number UNRESOLVED
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): '総人口に占める65歳以上の高齢者の割合は29.4%で過去最高…3,619万人'.
limitation: Comparator only.
decision_use: Denominator comparator for R7-E-A06.

exact_claim: Kokusen (2021-10-07): consumer centres had received about 500 subscription ('サブスク') consultations per month since FY2021, many from internet sign-ups, including cases where consumers believed they had already cancelled ('解約したはず!').
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): 'サブスクに関する相談が、2021年度以降、毎月500件程度寄せられています…契約内容等を正しく認識していないまま契約し、請求に気づいてトラブルになる'.
counterevidence: No later monthly count was found, so the trend after 2021 is UNKNOWN.
limitation: Five years old. 500/month (about 6,000 a year) against about 80-98k 定期購入 consultations a year reflects coding categories, not true incidence.
decision_use: J5 exists as a recognised complaint type ('I thought I cancelled'). The volume in Kokusen's 'サブスク' code is small relative to 定期購入.

exact_claim: Kokusen (2026-07-09) warns that deleting or uninstalling an app does not cancel a subscription, that free trials usually convert automatically, and advises consumers to check card and carrier-billing statements every month.
exact_locator: 見守り新鮮情報 第545号
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): 'アプリのアイコンを削除したり、アプリをアンインストールするだけでは解約とはなりません'; 'クレジットカードやキャリア決済等の明細は、毎月確認しましょう'.
limitation: Advisory, not incidence.
decision_use: B2: the official free workaround for J1/J5 is self-review of statements. J3 confusion (app deletion ≠ cancellation) is a routing and knowledge gap, not an execution gap.

exact_claim: Kokusen (2026-08-19) publicly named the monthly clothing-rental subscription Rcawaii (operator Gracegres) after about 1,600 consultations, including billing that continued after cancellation requests.
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): '月額制の洋服レンタルサービスに関する相談が寄せられている…注意喚起'; count about 1,600 seen in an earlier extract.
limitation: A single provider. Its conduct is the outlier that triggered a named warning, not the norm.
decision_use: J5/J6 failures concentrate in non-cooperative providers. There an on-behalf agent meets the same non-response, so the remedy is J6 (dispute, regulator, chargeback), not better execution.

exact_claim: Kokusen (2024-11-20) reports consultations from bereaved families who want to identify or cancel a deceased person's online subscriptions but cannot, because they lack the IDs and passwords.
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): '遺族が契約内容の確認や解約をしたくても、ID、パスワードの手がかりがないために手続きに困るケース'.
limitation: No counts. The bereavement process is provider-specific (S4).
decision_use: A distinct segment in which J1 (discovery without credentials) binds and the acting party is not the account holder. Kept separate (see report §A.4).

exact_claim: Okane-ko survey (2025-12, n=330 platform users): 61.8% currently subscribe. Of those, 50.5% had been auto-billed after a free or first-month-free trial they forgot to cancel, and 19.1% hold a barely used subscription they have not cancelled. About one in three have no habit of reviewing subscriptions.
population: Users of the Okane-ko personal-finance platform
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): 'サブスク契約者は61.8%で、そのうち50.5%が初月無料やお試し期間終了後の解約忘れによる自動課金を経験'; '「ほとんど使っていないのに解約し忘れている」…19.1%'.
counterevidence: ゼニエモン survey: half reviewed within a year (R7-E-A14).
limitation: Non-probability sample of finance-engaged users, run by a firm that sells financial advice. Small n.
decision_use: J1 (forgetting) is common even among finance-engaged users. It points to discovery and reminders (C01), not execution.

exact_claim: AZWAY survey (2026-06, n=300, ages 20-69): more than half had paid for a subscription they forgot to cancel.
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): 'サブスクの解約し忘れによって無駄に料金を払っていた経験がある人が半数を超えた'.
limitation: Exact share not visible ('半数超'). Panel and sponsor motives not checked. Small n.
decision_use: Second independent family for J1 forgetting (see R7-E-A16).

exact_claim: ゼニエモン survey (2025-07/08, n=400 via CrowdWorks): 79.0% use subscriptions (20s: 92.0%). The modal monthly subscription spend is ≤¥2,000. The modal review answer is 'not reviewed for over a year', but about half reviewed within the past year.
metric: Usage share; modal spend band; review recency
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): '79.0%が「利用している」…20代では92.0%'; '最も多かった回答は「2,000円以下」'; '回答者の半数が1年以内に契約状況を見直している'.
counterevidence: Okane-ko: about a third have no review habit (R7-E-A12).
limitation: Self-selected gig-work sample, probably younger and more online than the population. The spend distribution beyond the mode is not visible.
decision_use: Money at risk per user is modest: the modal total subscription spend is ≤¥2,000 a month, which caps the savings a consumer could attribute to the product.

exact_claim: The 65+ share of consumer-centre consultations (37.7%, FY2025) is 1.28 times the 65+ population share (29.4%, 2025).
limitation: Mixes a fiscal-year consultation share with a September population share. All topics, not subscriptions. Both inputs are reported_unopened.
decision_use: Comparator only.

exact_claim: Paying for forgotten or unused subscriptions is commonly reported among Japanese subscription users (direction only, not prevalence).
supporting_passage: Two independent private surveys (F10, F11) report it, and a Kokusen advisory (F06) warns about trial auto-conversion.
counterevidence: No probability-sample prevalence estimate exists in the extracts.
limitation: Only the direction is corroborated. The magnitude is not.
decision_use: J1 is real and common. That supports trackers and reminders, not execution.

exact_claim: CAA's expert committee on continuous contracts (interim summary, reported 2026-08-28 to 2026-09) proposes amending the Consumer Contract Act to prohibit obstructing cancellation of subscriptions and 定期購入: misrepresenting important matters, refusing or unreasonably delaying cancellation, and deceptive or intimidating conduct. Qualified consumer organisations could seek injunctions. A bill is targeted for as early as the next ordinary Diet session. Effort duties under consideration include reasonable cancellation methods, disclosure of cancellation conditions, contacts and methods, notice before auto-renewal, and notice of important term changes.
exact_locator: CAA expert committee interim summary (exact title/date UNRESOLVED; earlier extract: 2026-09-09)
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): Nikkei: 'サブスク解約妨害に規制…解約料は説明責任'; Kyodo: '重要事項のうそ…解約申し出の拒否や不当な遅延…'; earlier extracts: 適格消費者団体の差止請求; 来年の通常国会にも法案.
counterevidence: Final scope and timing are not decided. Effort duties (努力義務) are not prohibitions. Whether phone-only or complex flows will be covered is speculative (R7-S013 headline ends in 'か').
limitation: Primary committee documents not opened. All outlets report one process (F02).
decision_use: K1 (two-sided): it validates obstruction as a recognised harm, and from about 2027-28 it targets the exact frictions an execution service would monetise. It does not obviously address forgetting (J1) or platform/bundle routing (J3).

exact_claim: A DIME article reports that respondents use 2.3 subscription services on average and that a monthly cost under ¥3,000 is the most common band.
population: UNKNOWN (survey sponsor, sample and date not identified)
metric: Mean services per user; modal spend band
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): '現在利用しているサブスクサービスは平均2.3個で、月額費用は3000円未満が最多'.
limitation: Provenance unknown, so it cannot carry any decision.
decision_use: Not used. Recorded so it is not later mistaken for a verified average.

exact_claim: 2024 定期購入 consultations (89,044) are about 9.75% of FY2024 total consultations (913k). This is an order-of-magnitude comparator only, because a calendar-year count is divided by a fiscal-year total.
limitation: Period mismatch, and the 913k total is rounded. Not a valid share.
decision_use: 定期購入 is a top-tier complaint category (about one in ten consultations), not a niche.

exact_claim: On card statements, Apple charges appear under one descriptor (APPLE.COM/BILL) that covers App Store purchases, Apple's own subscriptions, in-app purchases and Family Sharing purchases. Identifying the specific subscription requires the Apple ID purchase history or subscription list.
population: App Store purchases charged to cards
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): '「apple com bill」はAppleが提供する各種サービスやアプリ購入に関する決済がクレジットカード明細に表示される際の公式請求名義'; 'ファミリー共有時は家族が利用した分も請求に含まれます'.
counterevidence: None found. Apple's own billing help page was not located.
limitation: Community and secondary sources.
decision_use: C1/C2/F1: card- or bank-transaction data cannot resolve platform-billed subscriptions to a provider, and a later APPLE.COM/BILL charge does not show which subscription persisted. J5 verification for this class needs Apple-side data (receipt e-mail or the user's subscription list).

exact_claim: The three carriers' billing portals list active continuous charges: docomo (d払い/ドコモ払い '継続課金一覧'), au (auかんたん決済 continuous-charge list) and SoftBank (My SoftBank 'まとめて支払い'). For docomo the extract says a 'details' link leads to the provider's site, where cancellation is done. For au it says services can be cancelled from the list page.
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): '「継続課金一覧」をタップすると現在契約中のサービスが確認できます'; 'auかんたん決済で契約中のサービスは継続課金一覧ページより解約できます'; '「詳細」をタップすると、サービス提供者のWebサイトへのリンクボタン…サービス提供者サイトで解約手続き'.
counterevidence: The au and docomo descriptions differ (cancel in the carrier portal vs at the provider). Resolve per provider in S4.
limitation: Partly secondary how-to text, and possibly dated.
decision_use: B2/C1: carriers already provide a free J1 list for this rail. A card statement shows only the phone-bill total, so card-based detection cannot see these subscriptions (R7-E-B06).

exact_claim: The Google Play Developer API lets the app's developer cancel a user's subscription server-side (purchases.subscriptionsv2.cancel; types USER_REQUESTED_STOP_RENEWALS and DEVELOPER_REQUESTED_STOP_PAYMENTS).
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): 'Developers can cancel a subscription server-side by calling purchases.subscriptionsv2.cancel'.
limitation: The capability belongs to the developer (merchant). Nothing found grants a third party such an API.
decision_use: D2: for Play-billed subscriptions no permitted machine route for a third party was found (no path found ≠ prohibition). The practical route is user self-service in Play (route B or self-service).

exact_claim: Developers cannot cancel a user's Apple App Store subscription. Only the user, through their Apple account, or Apple support can.
exact_locator: RevenueCat community 308; Apple Developer Forums thread 727298
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): 'it's impossible for the developer to cancel a user's Apple subscription'.
counterevidence: None found. Apple's own documentation stating this was not located.
limitation: Community statements.
decision_use: D2: App Store-billed subscriptions have no machine route for any party except the user or Apple, so execution is user-only (route B handoff at best).

exact_claim: Gym and fitness-club cancellation commonly requires a written form or an in-store visit. Reported trouble includes 'told by phone that a written form is required' and 'submitted the form in store, but told the cancellation was not processed'.
exact_locator: Kyoto pref 1294273032248; 見守り新鮮情報 484
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): '電話で退会を伝えたのに、書面が必要と言われた'; '来店して解約届を出したはずなのに、手続きが完了していないと言われた'; '書面で申請しないと解約や休会にならず、引き落としが続いてしまう場合'; 'キャンペーンなどの特典で契約した場合、一定期間は解約できない、解約違約金がかかるなどの条件が設けられていることがあります'.
counterevidence: None. Some chains offer online cancellation (to be checked per provider in S4).
limitation: No counts.
decision_use: Physical memberships are a candidate route D (in person) or C (written instruction). A J5 failure mode (form submitted, not processed) is documented.

exact_claim: Card- or bank-transaction detection sees platform-billed (APPLE.COM/BILL, Google Play) and carrier-billed subscriptions only as aggregate merchant lines, so it cannot identify, or verify the stop of, the individual subscriptions inside them.
population: Subscriptions billed via platform or carrier rails
supporting_passage: Inference from the descriptor and portal behaviour above.
counterevidence: Google Play's card descriptor may name the app (format not checked). Some PFM apps may parse receipt e-mails. Both are for S3.
limitation: Inference, not tested on data.
decision_use: C1: detection needs a second channel (e-mail receipts, platform screens or user entry) for the rails that the Apple/Google/carrier lists already cover. Makes B1 doubly important.

exact_claim: GEM Partners estimates Japan's subscription video (SVOD) market at about ¥601.7bn in 2025 (+14.3% YoY). Growth came from price increases and services per user (1.8 to 2.0), not user growth. Shares: Netflix 27.1%, U-NEXT 17.1%, Prime Video 12.1%.
metric: Market size (¥); services per user; spend share
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): '2025 market size … approximately 6,017 [億円] … 14.3% increase'; 'services per person from 1.8 to 2.0'; 'Netflix 27.1%, U-NEXT 17.1%, Prime Video 12.1%'.
limitation: A vendor estimate. The extract rendered the size as '6,017 billion yen', which is a unit error; 6,017億円 = ¥601.7bn is used here.
decision_use: Two subscriptions per SVOD user is a low count per user (G2). The top three hold 56.3% of spend (R7-E-B08), so a handful of playbooks covers most SVOD spend. That favours a cheap guide (C02) and is easy for incumbents to copy (I1).

exact_claim: The top three SVOD services hold 56.3% of 2025 SVOD spend (27.1 + 17.1 + 12.1).
limitation: Input shares are a vendor estimate.
decision_use: See R7-E-B07.

exact_claim: Sensor Tower and Adjust estimate Japan's mobile consumer app spend (App Store + Google Play) at $16.5bn in 2024, and mobile-game in-app spend at about $11bn for Aug 2024-Jul 2025.
population: App Store + Google Play consumer spend
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): 'Japan's mobile market generated $16.5 billion in consumer spend in 2024'; 'Japanese gamers spent $11 billion on in-app purchases … Aug 2024 to Jul 2025'.
limitation: The periods differ, so non-game spend cannot be computed by subtraction. Game IAP is mostly one-off purchases, not subscriptions.
decision_use: B1: platform-rail spend is dominated by games. No public split of Japanese subscriptions by billing rail was found (R7-E-B10).

exact_claim: No public survey or dataset was found that splits Japanese consumer subscriptions (count or spend) by billing rail: App Store, Google Play, carrier billing, card-on-file with the provider, bank debit or convenience-store payment.
exact_locator: Searches 2026-10-05: 'サブスク 支払い方法 アプリストア課金 … 割合', 'MMD研究所 サブスク 支払い方法', 'サブスク どこで契約 アプリ内課金 … 契約経路', 'ICT総研 動画配信 支払い方法'
supporting_passage: Search extracts stated that no such split was present in the results.
counterevidence: Paid industry reports (MMD, ICT総研, 矢野経済研究所) may hold it. They were not accessible.
limitation: Absence in search extracts is not absence of data.
decision_use: B1 and stop condition 1 cannot be tested with public data. The billing-rail mix of the target segment must be measured in primary research (E-design S8).

exact_claim: MMD Research (2025-07, n=25,000, ages 18-69): in the last month, 74.9% paid by cash, 53.0% by credit card and 46.7% by QR/barcode.
metric: Share using each method in the last month
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): '「現金」が74.9%と最も多く、次いで「クレジットカード」が53.0%、「QR・バーコード決済」が46.7%'.
limitation: General payments, not subscriptions.
decision_use: Comparator: about half of adults used a credit card in the month. A card-linked detection product's reachable base is a subset of the population before any linking friction.

exact_claim: Money Forward ME had 17.3M users as of October 2025.
exact_locator: Money Forward investor material (SBI seminar PDF), page UNKNOWN
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): 'マネーフォワード MEの利用者数は1,730万人です（2025年10月時点）'.
limitation: Registered users, not MAU. Paid premium users not disclosed in the extract.
decision_use: L1/H12: MF's distribution is the base on which a cheap 'cancel' feature would land. Compared with Moneytree's about 6.5M (R7-E-G07), MF is the larger channel. No population-share claim is made (denominator not sourced).

exact_claim: From 2025-08-05, Money Forward ME premium (standard) costs ¥540 a month or ¥5,940 a year by card, and ¥590 / ¥6,490 via App Store or Google Play. The asset-building course is ¥980 / ¥10,700.
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): 'スタンダードコース（月額プラン）：540円 … App Store/Google Play決済の場合 … 590円'.
limitation: Whether tax is included is not visible.
decision_use: G1: a consumer price anchor. Bank-linked tracking with a subscription report already costs ¥540 a month.

exact_claim: Money Forward ME's premium 'サブスクレポート' lists the previous month's subscription payments detected from card and bank statements, for named services such as Netflix, YouTube Premium, Disney+ and Hulu. Money Forward states that charges which cannot be told apart from other payments on the statement, such as App Store and carrier billing, are not currently supported.
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): 'App Store決済やキャリア決済の様に、明細の表示から他の支払いと区別ができないものは、現在対応ができておりません'.
limitation: The coverage count of named services is UNKNOWN. No cancellation function was mentioned.
decision_use: C2 (falsified for card/bank rails): the largest incumbent already detects card-rail subscriptions. It confirms R7-E-B06 for platform and carrier rails, whose own free lists already cover them.

exact_claim: Money Forward runs 『マネーフォワード 固定費の見直し』. It shows annual spend, expected savings and whether a review is needed for insurance, electricity, internet and phone, and includes its own electricity retail service 『マネーフォワード でんき』, whose customers get ME premium free while contracted.
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): '保険料、電気代、インターネット代、スマホ代の4つの費目で、年間支出額と想定削減金額、見直しの必要有無を確認'.
counterevidence: Current (2026) status of these services not checked.
limitation: 2023 release.
decision_use: H14/C08: the switching and fixed-cost model a startup would expand into is already run by the incumbent that holds the data.

exact_claim: Moneytree Grow, launched on iOS on 2019-08-29, costs ¥360 a month or ¥3,600 a year.
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): '月額360円または年額3,600円'.
limitation: Price after the MUFG acquisition not checked.
decision_use: G1: the cheapest bank-linked subscription list is ¥360 a month.

exact_claim: Moneytree Grow's 'サブスク一覧' shows, month by month, automatically retrieved subscription payments with amount, payment date and payment method. Whether users can add items manually, whether App Store or carrier-billed charges are covered, and whether any cancellation function exists were not visible. No cancellation function was found.
exact_locator: Moneytree help 9119773 (content not seen); xexeq topics32637
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): '自動取得されたサブスクサービスの支払い料金、支払日、支払い方法などを月々で表示'.

exact_claim: Under the Civil Code (Art. 99), a declaration an agent makes within their authority, showing it is for the principal, takes effect directly for the principal. Textbook doctrine distinguishes an agent (代理人, who decides) from a messenger (使者, who conveys or expresses the principal's own decision and needs no legal capacity). Authority may be granted through a mandate contract (委任, Art. 643).
exact_locator: Wikibooks 民法第99条; Crear commentary
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): '代理では代理人が意思決定者となるのに対し、使者では本人が意思決定者となる'; '委任契約（643条）のように明確に契約に基づいて代理権が授与される場合'.
limitation: Textbook summary. e-Gov text not opened. Whether a provider must accept either form is a separate question.
decision_use: E1: the operating design most consistent with the 退職代行 boundary is a messenger conveying the user's own final decision. Whether that suffices against each provider is for counsel (E5).

exact_claim: Practitioner commentary on resignation agencies (退職代行) holds that a non-lawyer business which only conveys the employee's own decision to resign acts as a messenger and does not breach Attorney Act Art. 72. Negotiating paid leave, unpaid wages or terms is non-lawyer legal practice. Penalty: up to 2 years' imprisonment or a ¥3M fine.
exact_locator: LegalOn resignation-agency; bengo4 n_19528; Money Forward contract basic 222
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): 'Simply delivering a resignation notice prepared by the client to the employer, acting as a messenger, would not constitute non-attorney practice'; 'engaging in negotiation over paid leave or unpaid wages constitutes non-attorney practice'.
counterevidence: Commentary, not a court ruling. Resignation is a unilateral right of the employee. Some subscription cancellations depend on terms, fees and deadlines that invite back-and-forth.
limitation: An analogy only. Consumer cancellation was not addressed by these sources.
decision_use: E1/E2: conveyance only; no negotiation, no fee or refund disputes, no retention bargaining. C06 (negotiation) and J6 sit on the wrong side of the analogy.

exact_claim: In late October 2025, Tokyo police searched Albatross Inc., operator of the resignation agency 'モームリ' (¥22,000 per full-time case), on suspicion of Attorney Act violations linked to referring clients to lawyers for fees. limitation: Media reports.
decision_use: E2: enforcement risk in the closest analogue industry is current. A cancellation service must not take referral fees from lawyers for dispute cases (J6) and must refer disputes only to free channels (188) or unpaid listings, pending counsel.

exact_claim: Whether Art. 72's 'other general legal matters' requires a dispute or doubt (事件性必要説) is contested in doctrine. The Supreme Court (1971-07-14) described the article's purpose as barring non-lawyers from intervening, for remuneration and as a business, in legal matters. A mandate contract breaching Art. 72 is void under Civil Code Art. 90 (Supreme Court 1963-06-13).
exact_locator: Wikibooks 弁護士法第72条; Miyake PDF (2026-08)
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): '事件性必要説と事件性不要説…見解が分かれています'; '弁護士法72条本文前段に抵触する委任契約は、民法第90条に照して無効'.
counterevidence: See R7-E-E05 (MOJ guideline applies an 事件性 test in one context).
limitation: Judgments not opened.
decision_use: E1: undisputed cancellations may fall outside Art. 72, but this is unsettled. If they do not, customer contracts could be void, which is also an economic risk (refunds).

exact_claim: MOJ's 2023-08-01 guidance on AI contract-review services states that a service risks breaching Art. 72 only if it is for remuneration, involves a matter with 事件性, and handles legal affairs requiring legal expertise. Ordinary contracts without a dispute were treated as lacking 事件性.
exact_locator: MOJ guidance (via LegalOn news 22; freee; DocuSign)
supporting_passage: Search-tool extract (paraphrase, not verbatim): '報酬目的・事件性・法律の専門知識に基づく法律事務という3要件をすべて満たす場合に、非弁行為にあたる可能性'; '事件性のない一般的な契約などは非弁行為にあたらない'.
counterevidence: The guidance addresses contract-review tools, not agents who act toward a counterparty.
limitation: Context-specific. Not opened.
decision_use: E1: the most recent official reasoning supports a narrow, undisputed-cancellation boundary, but it does not cover acting toward a provider. A counsel question, not a green light.
